resources.string: Step by step: where to tap and why
Your photos, files, notes and calendar stay on your own devices. This guide shows where to tap and why. Read a step, tap Try it, and do it on the real screen while the step stays in view.
Skip it now if you like. The guide is always in Settings › Guide, and each chapter opens on its own.
Some parts of Tetra need your permission. Each page says what it is for. Tap Allow, then answer Android’s question. You can say no now and allow it here later.
Files, Notes, Office, Calendar, Timer and Maps keep everything in one Tetra folder on this device. Android opens a page with one switch: turn it on, then go back.
Photos shows your pictures and videos, finds faces and places, and sends them to your computer. Choose Allow all: with only some chosen, Photos shows only those.
Reminders, timers and sync tell you things with a notification. Without it a reminder cannot ring.
A reminder or a timer rings at the minute you set, even while the phone sleeps. On most phones this is already allowed.
Scanner photographs documents, Codes reads QR codes, and pairing with a computer scans its code. Choose While using the app.
Contacts shows the people in your phone and can keep a copy of yours there, so calls and other apps know their names.
Phone makes and answers calls and shows your call history, and your computer can call through this phone. A tablet without a SIM does not need it.
Data counts how much mobile data each app uses. Android shows a list: find Tetra, tap it and turn on the switch.
Maps shows where you are and guides you there, and Data needs it to see the names of Wi-Fi networks around you. Choose While using the app.
Each picture on Home opens an applet. Tap Files to see your files.
Tap the pencil at the top. Each part gets a frame and two small buttons, and taps open nothing until you are done.
Hold a part until it lifts, then drag it to any cell. The others make room.
Tap the arrows on a part. Each tap makes it large, medium, small and large again: large shows more inside it, small is just its picture.
Tap the eye to hide a part you do not use. Hidden parts wait under the grid: tap one to bring it back. Its reminders and timers go on.
Tap Done when Home looks right. Reset puts it back as it was at the start.
Tap a folder to go in and a file to open it. The arrow at the top goes back out.
Hold a file until it is ticked, then tap others to add them. Holding chooses; a short tap opens.
With files chosen, tap Move (the arrow) or Copy (two pages) in the bar at the bottom. Copy leaves the first one where it was.
Tap a folder to go into it, Up to go back out, then Move here.
Tap the three dots next to a file for everything about that one file: rename, share, tags, colour and Trash.
Tap New in the bar at the bottom for a folder, a text file, or a Words, Tables or Slides document, right in the folder you are in.
What you delete goes to Trash first. Swipe up on the bar at the bottom for Files tools, tap Trash, choose what you want back and tap Restore.
You do not need a computer. Without one, everything stays on this device, and you can pair later.
On the computer, open Devices › Add a device: Tetra shows a code. Here, open Local Sync from Home, tap Scan a code and point the camera at it.
Settings › Appearance changes the language, dark or light, and what Home shows.
Type in the search at the top of Settings to find any setting by its name.
Tetra uses the same small pictures everywhere. Here is each one and what it does.
New: a folder, a note, an event…
Edit or Rename, depending on where it is: Home is edited, a file is renamed
More: everything about this one item
Share it with another app or person
Copy: a second one goes there, the first stays
Move: it goes there and leaves here
To Trash: it can still come back
Tags: your own labels, to find things later
Favourite: kept at hand under Favourites
Hide it from view; nothing is deleted
Drag or swipe up here for more
A list of choices: tap to pick one
Look again for what is new
Scan a code with the camera
Show this device’s code to pair it
